key_insight: A unified bilevel framework tunes mesh-free PDE solver designs using held-out validation residuals, with error analysis linking optimization approximations to solution accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a common tuning strategy for representation, residual weighting, and regularization across several mesh-free solver families.
method: Fit solution coefficients on training collocation residuals; optimize solver-design parameters on validation residuals.
Approximate lower-level solutions with finite, warm-started damped Gauss–Newton updates.
Use the damped Gauss–Newton matrix to initialize and precondition adjoint iterations, with bounds separating key hypergradient errors.
evidence_signal: Experiments on several nonlinear PDEs, including a high-dimensional problem, report accuracy and efficiency across Kansa, random-feature/extreme-learning-machine, and physics-informed neural network solvers.
watch_item: The hypergradient guarantees are local, so practical reliability requires attention to lower-level convergence, damping, adjoint residuals, and validation sampling.
paper_title: A Validation-Driven Bilevel Optimization Method for Mesh-Free PDE Solvers and Its Error Analysis
